solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Fish's batter is rubbish

parts.note: the cod is a fish, here with its possessive S kept
to batter is to thump, to wallop

explanation.surface: A chip-shop complaint: the battered fish served up is no good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'batter' looks like the coating on fried fish, but it is the verb meaning to hit hard. The 'S of Fish's stays in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang synonym: nonsense or worthless talk is called rubbish.

clue.text: Cross after ring has one side deformed and become rusty

indicators.note: after puts the cross letter following the ring letter

parts.note: a ring is round, the letter O
X is a cross
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: deformed says the letters of side are twisted out of shape

explanation.surface: A cross and ring, part misshapen, going rusty: an old piece of jewellery.
explanation.definitionFit: Chemistry: iron combining with oxygen corrodes, so to rust is to combine with oxygen.

clue.text: Almost everyone fitted in son's room

indicators.note: fitted in says the shortened word goes inside the letters for son

parts.note: son gives its own letters, the 's a link

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: everyone is all

explanation.surface: Nearly the whole family squeezed into a son's bedroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'room' is the definition, a salon being a grand reception room rather than only a hairdresser's.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a reception room or drawing room in a grand house.

clue.text: Sticking notice in this place by a set of books

parts.note: an ad is a notice or advertisement
here means in this place
NT, the New Testament, is a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Posting a notice near a shelf of books.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as adjectives: clinging or holding fast to something is adhesive, cleaving.

clue.text: Measure of changes in Nato's international organisation

parts.note: a league is an old measure of distance, about three miles

indicators.note: changes means the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of Nato with its S

explanation.surface: A statement that NATO's changes are measured by an international body.
explanation.definitionFit: The interwar body founded in 1920 to keep world peace, the forerunner of the UN.

clue.text: The force to cut up diamonds

indicators.note: up in a down clue means read from bottom to top

parts.note: to lop is to cut off
ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: Someone plans to slice diamonds with force.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: the police service is commonly called the force.

clue.text: Drunk with women in study

indicators.note: in says the letter for women is placed within the word for a drunk

parts.note: a sot is a drunkard

explanation.surface: Someone tipsy in the company of women in a study room.
explanation.definitionFit: British school slang: to cram or revise hard is to study intensively.

clue.text: Topless clean girls dancing — one should send out a warning!

definitions.text: one should send out a warning!

indicators.note: dancing sets the letters moving into new order
topless means the first letter of clean is removed

explanation.surface: A racy scene of topless girls dancing, with a call for a warning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topless' strips CLEAN to LEAN; 'dancing' rearranges LEAN GIRLS.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone transmitting signals, such as a railway or army operator, sends alerts.

clue.text: This number's set

parts.note: the clue is numbered eight, so a set of this number is a group of eight

explanation.walkthrough: 'This number' refers to the clue's own number, 8.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of eight performers or items is so called.

clue.text: Waste talent? Not at first

indicators.note: not at first tells us to drop the opening letter of the word for talent

parts.note: talent or ability is skill

explanation.surface: A lament about squandered ability, though not from the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as verbs: to waste or slay someone is to murder them, an American slang sense.

clue.text: Crumpet arrives — they could be turned on tonight!

definitions.text: they could be turned on tonight!

parts.note: crumpet is old British slang for the head
to light on or upon somewhere is to land or arrive there

explanation.surface: An arrival of attractive company, said with a saucy wink about getting turned on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crumpet' suggests the toasted teacake or the slang for attractive women; here it is old slang for the head, as in 'barmy in the crumpet'.
explanation.definitionFit: Car lamps are switched on after dark, so these are things one might turn on this evening.

clue.text: Broke — we/I earn not a sausage

indicators.note: broke suggests the letters are smashed and rearranged
not says the letter A is left out of the pool before rearranging

explanation.surface: A broke couple complaining that between them they don't earn a sausage, nothing at all.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove A from WEIEARN, then rearrange the remaining six letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a frankfurter-style sausage is called a wiener, especially in America.

clue.text: Immoral aunt — she's perverted outside clubs

indicators.note: outside says the scrambled letters sit around the club abbreviation
perverted means twisted, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of aunt and she, the 's standing for is as a link
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: A scandalised report about a wayward aunt carrying on outside nightclubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perverted' gives UNHASTE, which goes around C; 'clubs' suggests nightclubs but is the card suit.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: lacking sexual restraint or chastity is being immoral.

clue.text: A manner of singing bass? The Spanish are able to

parts.note: B is the music abbreviation for bass
el is the Spanish word for the
to be able to is can

explanation.surface: A question whether Spanish singers can manage a bass part.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian term for an operatic style prizing beautiful tone and agile phrasing, literally 'fine song'.

clue.text: Where you might find miner's indifferent about Michael Caine film

indicators.note: about says the word for indifferent wraps around the film title

parts.note: cold means indifferent or unfeeling
Alfie is the 1966 film starring Michael Caine

explanation.surface: A miner showing no interest in a Michael Caine film.
explanation.definitionFit: Coal miners work in an area rich in seams of coal.

clue.text: Vegetable's caught in flipping rake, Eleanor!

indicators.note: flipping says the hidden letters are read backwards
caught in says the letters are trapped inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An exasperated gardener tells Eleanor a vegetable has got stuck in the rake.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Vegetable's caught' as the definition, but 'caught in' is the hiding signal and the 's is a link; 'flipping' doubles as an exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a long white onion-family plant grown as a vegetable, the emblem of Wales.

clue.text: Group of armed policemen hit char on motorway

indicators.note: on in a down clue puts the first part above the next

parts.note: to swat is to hit
char is British slang for tea
M is the abbreviation for motorway, as in the M1

explanation.surface: A cleaning lady struck on the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'char' looks like a cleaner or to scorch, but it is slang for tea.
explanation.definitionFit: An American-style specialist police unit trained for armed operations.

clue.text: Run and catch tailless bird

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run

indicators.note: tailless means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: to catch a sound is to hear it

explanation.surface: Chasing down and catching a bird that has lost its tail.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a large flightless South American bird resembling an ostrich.

clue.text: In church you could see this twit swallowing wine? On the contrary

definitions.text: In church you could see this

indicators.note: swallowing says one word goes inside the other
on the contrary reverses the roles, so the wine swallows the twit

parts.note: hock is a German white wine
an ass is a fool, a twit

explanation.surface: A fool gulping communion wine in church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the contrary' reverses the surface's roles: the wine is the swallower. Hock is a German white wine from the Rhine.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a kneeling cushion found in church pews.

clue.text: How we might receive current affairs from young head of staff — with spin

definitions.text: How we might receive current affairs

parts.note: young means new

indicators.note: head of picks the first letter of staff

parts.note: to reel is to spin or whirl

explanation.surface: A newsroom image: news delivered by a youthful boss with a slick spin put on it.
explanation.definitionFit: Short cinema films of current events were how audiences once got their news.

clue.text: Pete is excited about opening of love letter

indicators.note: about says the scrambled letters go around the opening letter
excited means stirred up, so the letters are rearranged
opening of picks the first letter of love

explanation.surface: Pete is thrilled at opening a love letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excited' gives EPISTE, which goes around L.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a formal or literary letter, as in the New Testament letters.

clue.text: Criminal is rat, beginning to talk for Constable, perhaps

indicators.note: criminal suggests the letters are corrupted and rearranged
beginning to picks the first letter of talk

explanation.surface: A criminal informer starts talking to a police constable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Constable' is John Constable, the English landscape painter, not a policeman.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: John Constable was a famous English landscape painter.

clue.text: Court disaster: King's head is fat or revolting

indicators.note: revolting means rising up, so the letters are overturned and rearranged
the head of King's is its first letter

explanation.surface: A rude remark about a portly monarch, perhaps on a pub sign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolting' looks like disgusting, but it signals rearranging K, IS, FAT, OR.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to invite trouble by provoking it is to court disaster.

clue.text: Poor old boy's eaten by goat

indicators.note: eaten by says the old boy letters go inside the word for a fool

parts.note: a goat is a silly person, a twit
OB is the abbreviation for old boy, the 's a link

explanation.surface: A sad farmyard tale of an elderly man devoured by a goat.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: cheap, shoddy or worthless things are poor quality.

clue.text: Band in studio as I speak

indicators.note: in says the answer sits within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A musician says the band is in the studio right now.
explanation.walkthrough: Oasis was a leading 1990s British rock band.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the Manchester rock group led by the Gallagher brothers.

clue.text: Player enjoyed these aces

parts.note: Gary Player, the South African golfer, scored aces, golf's single-stroke completions of a hole

explanation.surface: A card or tennis player happily dealing or serving aces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Player' is the golfer Gary Player; in golf an ace is a hole completed with the tee shot.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf a hole won with one stroke is called an ace.

clue.text: Ill will leaving parking place

indicators.note: leaving says the parking letter departs from the word

parts.note: spite is ill will
P is the abbreviation for parking on road signs

explanation.surface: Resentment as a driver vacates a parking spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a location or plot of ground is a place.

clue.text: Finally slaps child — a sign one's lost one's grip?

definitions.text: a sign one's lost one's grip?

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of slaps

parts.note: a kid is a child

explanation.surface: A parent finally smacking a child, read as a sign they have lost control.
explanation.definitionFit: Tyres that lose traction slide, so this sliding motion shows grip is gone.

clue.text: Time to request team's changed before manager finally becomes a slave driver

indicators.note: before places the preceding letters ahead of what follows

parts.note: to request is to ask

indicators.note: changed means the letters of team's are rearranged
finally picks the last letter of manager

explanation.surface: A sports story: the team changed before the manager turns into a harsh boss.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone imposing heavy work on others is a harsh, demanding overseer.
